```text
Back Rank Mate

```

### 2. The Scholar's Mate
A classic opening trap targeting the weak f7 square, usually occurring in the first four moves of the game.

```text
Scholar's Mate
r1bqkbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4p3/2B1P3/5Q2/PPPP1PPP/RNB1K1NR w KQkq - 2 3
Qxf7#
```

### 3. The Arabian Mate
A pattern typically involving a Rook and a Knight. The Knight on f6 protects the Rook on g8 and covers the escape square h7.

```text
Arabian Mate
7k/7p/5N2/8/8/8/6R1/7K w - - 0 1
Rg8#
```

### 4. Reversed Fool's Mate
In this scenario, Black has weakened their King's diagonal (f7/g8) fatally early in the game, allowing the White Queen to deliver mate.

```text
Reversed Fool's Mate
rnbqkbnr/ppppp2p/8/5pp1/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/RNBQKBNR w KQkq - 0 3
Qh5#
```

```text

6rk/7p/8/6N1/B7/8/8/7K w - - 0 1
Nf7#
```

### 6. Promotion Mate
An endgame scenario where a White pawn advances to the 8th rank, promotes to a Queen (or Rook), and simultaneously delivers checkmate.

```text
Promotion Mate
7k/P7/7K/8/8/8/8/8 w - - 0 1
a8=Q#
```

### 7. The Ladder Mate
Also known as the "Lawnmower Mate," typically performed with two Rooks (or Queen and Rook) rolling the King to the edge of the board.

```text

k7/8/K7/1R6/8/8/1R6/8 w - - 0 1
Ra2#
```

### 8. Battery Mate (Queen & Bishop)
White creates a "battery" where the Queen is supported by a Bishop to deliver mate on a square adjacent to the King, usually g7 or h7.

```text
Battery Mate
6k1/5ppp/2B5/8/8/8/8/6QK w - - 0 1
Qg7#
```

### 9. Epaulette Mate

```text
Epaulette Mate
3rkr2/8/5K2/4Q3/8/8/8/8 w - - 0 1
Qe7#
```

### 10. Pawn Mate
A satisfying mate where the humblest piece delivers the final blow. In this setup, the White King restricts the Black King, and the Pawn delivers the checkmate.

